title.name: Pax Avant
title.subtitle: Shepherds of Roncal and Barétous
menu.easy.note: Grass lasts longer, flocks stay closer and arrows point to lost sheep.
menu.normal.note: The real mountain: you have to share well.
menu.solo.note: You are Roncal. The computer is Barétous, and helps if you trust each other.
menu.duo.note: Player 1: Roncal. Player 2: Barétous. You win or lose together!
intro.1: Every summer, shepherds from Roncal (Navarre) and Barétous (Béarn, in France) take their flocks up to the pastures on the border.
intro.2: Long ago they quarrelled over grass and water. When a pasture was eaten bare, both valleys went hungry.
intro.3: So they made an agreement, usually dated 1375: share the mountain, and meet every 13 July at the San Martín stone.
outro.1: The ceremony still takes place every 13 July, and the mayors still say "Pax avant": peace from now on.
outro.2: You can go and see it at the San Martín stone, high above the Belagua valley. Good neighbours share!
brief.title: One season on the mountain
brief.goal: Take your flock up in spring, look after it in summer and bring it home in autumn. Share the grass and the water.
brief.cpu: Barétous (square mark): played by the computer
brief.buttons: Stick: walk · [A] whistle the dog · [B] ring the bell · [C] gate, trough, fire, lamb
week.label: Week {n} of {of}
goal.moveUp.title: Up to the high pastures
goal.moveUp.text: Open the pen with [C] and lead the sheep up to the high grass.
goal.graze.title: Well-fed sheep
goal.graze.text: Find green grass. If a pasture turns brown, move to another.
goal.storm.title: Everyone under a roof
goal.storm.text: A storm is coming. When the warning comes, take the flocks to a shelter.
goal.night.title: A night with nobody lost
goal.night.text: Light fires with [C]. Wolves are scared off by dogs, bells and fire.
goal.drought.title: Water for everyone
goal.drought.text: Only the shared spring is left. Fill both troughs with [C] and share.
goal.moveDown.title: Everyone home
goal.moveDown.text: The cold is coming. Bring the flocks down to their pens before the week ends.
tip.gate: Stand by the pen gate and press [C] to open it.
tip.bell: [B] rings the bell: your sheep come to you. Walk slowly and they follow.
tip.whistle: [A] whistles the dog: it goes round the nearest sheep and pushes them the way you face.
tip.up: The high pastures are up at the top, by the border.
tip.grass: Green grass feeds. Brown grass takes a very long time to grow back.
tip.share: If both flocks eat the same pasture, it runs out fast. Share the mountain out!
tip.trust: Helping the other valley builds trust. With trust, the shared shelter opens.
tip.water: Sheep drink at the troughs. Fill them at the spring with [C].
tip.fire: Night has fallen. Light the fires with [C] to keep the wolves away.
tip.drought: Drought: the valley springs have dried up.
tip.down: Autumn is here. Graze the low pastures, then head home.
tip.close: When the sheep are inside, close the gate with [C].
msg.stormWarn: Storm in {n}s! Take the flocks to a shelter.
msg.wolf: A wolf is heading for the {valley} flock! Scare it off with the dog, the bell or fire.
msg.wolfHelped: Thanks for seeing off the wolf!
msg.wolfLeaves: The wolf gets bored and leaves
msg.lamb: A {valley} lamb is lost. Pick it up with [C] and carry it to its flock.
msg.dry: The valley springs are dry. Only the shared spring in the middle is left.
msg.fog: Fog: sheep lose their way. Keep an eye on them!
msg.snow: Snow! The sheep want to be in their pens.
msg.shelterOpenText: The valleys trust each other: the shared shelter and the neighbours’ huts are now open to all.
results.title: End of the season
ceremony.0: 13 July. The mayors shake hands, but the mountain is sad. Next year will be better.
ceremony.1: 13 July. The mayors lay their hands one on another on the stone and say "Pax avant".
ceremony.2: 13 July. A party on the pass! Both valleys celebrate a good summer together.
ceremony.3: 13 July. The best party in years! Music, dancing and very good neighbours.
ceremony.cows: As the agreement says, Barétous hands three cows to Roncal.

fact.treaty: Roncal and Barétous made an agreement to share pastures and water. It is usually dated 1375, and it is still kept.
fact.arbiters: It is said the agreement was settled by arbiters from the Ansó valley in Aragón, after years of quarrels over pasture.
fact.stone: The San Martín stone stands on a mountain pass, right on the border between Spain and France.
fact.gesture: At the ceremony, the mayors lay their hands one on another on the stone and say "Pax avant": peace from now on.
fact.cows: Every year Barétous hands three cows to Roncal, as the agreement says. That is why it is called the Tribute of the Three Cows.
fact.oldest: It is often said to be one of the oldest treaties in Europe that is still in force.
fact.transhumance: In winter, Roncal shepherds walked their flocks south to the Bardenas Reales. Moving flocks with the seasons is called transhumance.
fact.cheese: Roncal cheese is made from sheep’s milk. It is said to be the first Spanish cheese with a protected designation of origin.
fact.mayors: The Roncal mayors come to the ceremony in their traditional dress: dark and solemn, with a cloak.
fact.today: The ceremony takes place every 13 July at the San Martín stone, above the Belagua valley. Anyone can go and watch.
fact.commons: A pasture eaten down to the earth takes a long time to recover. Sharing and resting pastures keeps the mountain healthy.
